attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his hot take on his Substack, in his own voice.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense judgement about GPT-5 at launch. The normalisation keeps both parts: no huge leap, and the comparison to what people long expected. The 'fans will rejoice' clause is rhetorical framing.

contract.note: The plain reading (no broad dramatic gain over the pre-launch frontier, not a claim of zero progress) is ordinary and fits his 'still part of the pack' context. To support the claim, the contract requires both an incremental result and documented pre-launch expectations, which is fair given his wording.

evidence.note: Independent launch-day test across eight evals. GPT-5 High sets a new high (68), but the firm says the gain over o3 is not comparable to earlier generational jumps. This supports the incremental half only, and it is a single evaluator.
OpenAI's own launch disclosure claims state-of-the-art results across several areas. This is interested company evidence. It shows gains, not a dramatic leap over o3-class models.
Altman's 2024 pre-launch remark that GPT-5 would be better across the board. It documents an expectation one executive promoted, not what people generally expected, and gives no magnitude.

reviews.rationale: Independent testing (e1) suggests an incremental advance over the pre-launch frontier, which fits 'not a huge leap'. The contract also requires documented pre-launch expectations of a substantially larger leap. The packet has only one executive's remark (e3), which the contract says cannot establish general expectations, and the packet itself lists this as a gap. The company claims in e2 don't establish a broad dramatic leap. The support condition is not fully met and nothing establishes contradiction, so the outcome is unresolved.
